subject: mathematics
concept: Understanding the structure of a logical argument: definitions, postulates, and theorems
source_inspiration: adapted from Japan MEXT Courses of Study sequencing principles — original content, not copied text

exercise.concrete: Student sorts statement cards into 'definition,' 'assumed true (postulate),' and 'proven true (theorem)' categories
exercise.pictorial: Student matches a geometric statement to its correct category
exercise.abstract: Student explains the difference between a definition, a postulate, and a theorem

misconception_flags: treats a postulate (assumed) as if it required proof like a theorem

interest_binding: exercise regenerated using student's stated interest profile
